paper_metadata.title: Ultrastrong nanocrystalline oxide-dispersion-strengthened ferritic alloy with exceptional thermal stability

evidence.quote: a novel Zr-doped nanocrystalline 14YWTZ ferritic ODS alloy (Fe – 14Cr – 3W- 0.4Ti-0.8Zr-0.3Y 2 O 3 ) was prepared by mechanical alloying and high-pressure consolidation techniques.
For comparison, we also fabricated an ODS alloy without Zr addition (14YWT).

The 14YWTZ alloyed powders with a nominal composition of Fe – 14Cr – 3W-0.4Ti-0.8Zr-0.3Y 2 O 3 (wt%) were prepared by mechanically alloying the mixture of high-purity elemental Fe, Cr, W, Ti and Zr powders (Alfa Aesar, 99.9% pure, 200 mesh) and Y 2 O 3 nanoparticles (Alfa Aesar, 99.5% pure, with an average particle size of 20 nm).

evidence.quote: The consolidated NC alloy rolled at 800 ◦ C has an ultrahigh yield strength of 2730 MPa, which is the highest yield strength among the reported ferrite ODS alloys.
However, a high yield strength of 2270 MPa is still retained for the alloy rolled at 1000 ◦ C.
A high relative density of 99.5% is obtained for the consolidated bulk alloy, demonstrating the effectiveness of the high-pressure consolidation technique on powder densification process.
Consequently, dispersed strengthening of 543 ± 429 MPa is obtained for the annealed NC 14YWTZ alloy.

The Hall-Petch coefficient of 538 MPa ̅̅̅̅̅̅ ̅ μ m √ and grain size of 59 ± 16 nm were used for calculation, and a Hall-Petch strengthening of 2216 ± 300 MPa was obtained for the annealed NC 14YWTZ alloy.

The outstanding strength of the present NC 14YWTZ ferritic ODS alloys primarily originates from the Hall-Petch strengthening of the NC matrix, distinguishing them from conventional ODS alloys strengthened by dislocation forest and/or dispersed particles.
Thus, the strong kinetic pinning effect of NPs on grain boundary migration should contribute to the high thermal stability of the present NC 14YWTZ alloy.

The NPs are homogeneously distributed in the matrix. Besides, the grain boundary segments between the inter-granular NPs (as indicated by the red arrows) are observed to be significantly bowed out, revealing a remarkable interaction between the NPs and GBs.
revealing significant segregation of W, Cr, C and O, and slight segregation of Mn at the GBs. Besides, despite the low doping amount, Zr, Ti and Y are also observed to be enriched at GBs.
The high consolidation pressure (4 GPa) endows the bulk nanocrystalline 14YWTZ alloy with a nearly full relative density (~99.5%) and a reasonable tensile elongation.

As a consequence, the dislocation forest strengthening (σ ρ ) to the mechanical properties is negligible, whereas the dispersed strengthening from the NPs-dislocation interactions should be considered.
